I tried everything you mentioned here but her issue is that she has a small mouth. She can't even hold a pacifier in her mouth properly. I ended up going to exclusively pumping and can now pump enough for her to be 100% breastmilk fed. I gotta hand it to you all for the help.

You're welcome. That's great that she's getting your milk! That's truly an amazing effort and good on for you doing it. Exclusively pumping can be sustained long term, although i have no experience with it (only pumping to supplement) there are facebook groups and other resources for support from others in the same boat or specific advice.

If you want to you can always try her at the breast in intervals (once a fortnight or month maybe) to check how her mouth is growing (don't do it when engorged!). Converting to exclusive breastfeeding likely won't just happen as soon as her mouth is big enough but it is possible. There are many babies that have been exclusively tube fed since birth that have ended up exclusively breastfed, and that is a much harder journey than from bottle fed to breast.

If you do decide to try to breastfeed her again in future she may be used to the bottle's fast release and give up quickly because your milk doesn't flow instantly or as quickly as a bottle. Pumping just enough to start the let down prior to feeding may help or a supplementer may be useful.

Best wishes no matter how your feeding journey goes, you are a good mum for trying so hard.
